DTR · TALK ABOUT A SCENE

Both Doors, One Truth

STS-HS9-L4-1400P-HSELA910-CYP-AAD-01 • HS English Grades 9 and 10 • Central Idea and How It Develops from Details
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
A Choose Your Path story gives you two doors, but a good one gives you the same truth through either. Nia's group is building theirs from four details stitched on a quilt: an empty chair, a packed bag, an open door, one letter. In the story quilt tradition carried through the African diaspora, no square means much alone, and the whole cloth means everything. The teacher is painting the arrow before anyone has agreed which way it should point.
If a reader walked through DOOR ONE instead of DOOR TWO, which of the four details would still have to be in the story for the central idea to survive?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
What is Nia doing?
Look at the picture. Justify what Nia is doing, then argue what her group is about to decide and what evidence supports you.
2
What is Kofi holding?
Look at the picture. Justify what Kofi is holding, then argue why a storyteller in this room would need it.
3
What is the teacher doing?
Look at the picture. Justify what the teacher is doing, then argue what her work tells you about the choice the class faces.
4
What room is this? How do you know?
Look at the picture. Justify what room this is, then argue why this room is the right setting for this activity.
5
Tell me about the quilt on the wall.
Look at the picture. Justify what the quilt shows, then argue how separate details can add up to one central idea.
6
What is Zora wearing?
Look at the picture. Justify what Zora has on, then argue how each person's task builds one shared piece of work.
Record an answer for each question, then submit.
Content alignment: CCSS.ELA-LITERACY.RL.9-10.2 — Determine a central idea and analyze in detail its development, including how it emerges from specific details. ELD (Speaking — official ELPAC “Talk About a Scene”): PI.A.1, PII.B.3, PII.B.4, PII.B.5.
